high.title: Fed About to Raise Interest Rates?
high.summary: The Federal Reserve's hawkish shift is creating significant implications for global monetary policy and Vietnamese markets. At the recent FOMC meeting, the Fed maintained its easing stance with forecasts for one rate cut this year and another next year, but Chairman Jerome Powell emphasized this depends entirely on inflation actually declining. Market probabilities have dramatically shifted - the likelihood of Fed rate cuts in 2026 has dropped to just 37% from 72% at end-2025, while rate hike probability has surged to 45% from 11%. This hawkish global central bank pivot includes Australia raising rates, Japan signaling increases, and the UK viewing hikes as more likely than cuts. For Vietnamese markets, this creates upward pressure on global bond yields and strengthens USD, potentially pressuring VND and forcing SBV to consider more defensive monetary policy. Vietnamese government bond yields could face selling pressure as capital flows toward higher-yielding USD assets. Fund managers should monitor how this Fed pivot affects VND stability and whether SBV needs to adjust its policy stance to defend the currency while supporting domestic growth.

high.title: Four Major Banks Raise Deposit Rates, Some Terms Up 1.2%/Year
high.summary: Agribank has significantly raised deposit rates across multiple terms, with the 24-month term jumping dramatically from 5.3% to 6.5% annually - a massive 1.2 percentage point increase that now represents the bank's highest rate. Shorter terms saw 0.2 percentage point increases, while 12-18 month terms rose 0.7 points to 5.9%. This follows similar moves by Vietnam's other three largest state-owned banks (Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV), indicating coordinated monetary tightening across the banking system. The deposit rate increases suggest banks are competing more aggressively for funding amid potential liquidity tightening or loan demand growth. For bond markets, higher deposit rates make government bonds less attractive unless yields rise accordingly. This rate environment could signal upward pressure on Vietnamese government bond yields and potential SBV policy adjustments. The synchronized nature across major banks suggests system-wide funding pressures rather than individual bank issues, pointing to broader monetary conditions that could affect VND funding costs and credit availability.

high.title: Additional Banks Raise Interest Rates - With 350 Million VND, How Much Interest From Savings?
high.summary: BVBank has raised interest rates by 0.2-0.35 percentage points, with 6-month+ terms now offering 6.6-7.2% annually. Vikki Bank offers up to 8.4% for deposits over 999 billion VND, while Cake by VPBank provides 7.7-7.9% for 6-10 month terms. This continues March's trend of widespread rate hikes across commercial banks including Techcombank, VPBank, MB Bank, SHB, and Sacombank, with some banks like PG Bank pushing 6-month rates above 7% annually. The competitive deposit rate environment indicates banks' need for funding amid potential credit growth or liquidity management pressures. For Vietnamese bond markets, these elevated deposit rates create yield competition that could pressure government bond demand unless yields adjust upward correspondingly. This widespread rate increase across both state and private banks suggests system-wide funding cost pressures that could influence SBV monetary policy decisions and VND money market rates.

medium.title: Extremely Good News: Leaders of 2 Major US Stock Exchanges Share Same Expectation with Vietnamese Enterprises
medium.summary: Deputy PM Nguyen Hoa Binh visited NASDAQ and NYSE, with both exchanges expressing interest in partnering with Vietnam's International Financial Center development. This signals potential capital market cooperation and improved international access for Vietnamese companies.

medium.title: Wife of MB General Director Purchases Large Amount of Shares
medium.summary: Ms. Le Thi Hong Phan, wife of MB's CEO, purchased 2 million MBB shares between March 19-23, spending approximately 51 billion VND. Combined with her husband's holdings, the family now owns nearly 10 million shares (0.124% stake), showing management confidence in the bank's prospects.

medium.title: SHB Announces Record Date for Rights Offering to Existing Shareholders
medium.summary: SHB received approval for public offering of over 459 million shares to existing shareholders at 10:100 ratio, priced at 12,500 VND per share. The bank plans total capital increase to 53.442 trillion VND through multiple issuances including private placement and ESOP programs.

medium.title: Gold Prices This Morning March 26
medium.summary: SJC and ring gold prices are quoted at 170.5-173.5 million VND per tael across major brands like DOJI and PNJ. Bao Tin Minh Chau maintains higher quotes at 172.5-175.0 million VND per tael, with some stores temporarily closed for regulatory compliance verification.

medium.title: Has the Worst Period for Stock Market Passed?
medium.summary: VN-Index gained 67 points over two sessions, recovering from early week gap-down opening. Improved sentiment reflects cooling Middle East tensions and declining oil prices, reducing inflation and USD strength pressures on Vietnamese markets and monetary policy.
